title: Disclaimer
excerpt: Money, health, engineering and legal results are estimates — here is exactly where each one stops being reliable.
content:
Every calculator on this site is an estimate built from a documented formula. This page says, plainly, where the limits are — not to cover the site, but because a result you cannot place in context is a result you should not act on.

The short version: the arithmetic is right, the world it describes is more complicated than the arithmetic. Each page names its assumptions; this page says why they matter.

Money

Loan, mortgage, investment, savings and tax calculators reproduce standard formulas. Real statements differ: interest accrues on your lender's schedule rather than on a neat monthly grid, fees are charged in ways the formula cannot see, rounding happens at a different point, and tax rules change and depend on where you live, how you earn and what else you owe.

Treat the output as a planning figure. Compare it with an official statement or a lender's own illustration before committing to anything. Nothing on this site is a quotation, an offer of credit, or investment advice, and no result here takes account of your circumstances in the way a licensed adviser would.

Health

Health calculators — BMI, body surface area, dosage, pregnancy dates, renal function, risk scores — are educational. They use population-level formulas, not your individual clinical picture. They are not a diagnosis, a prescription, a substitute for a clinician who has examined you, or a reason to change a medication.

Where a calculator is used in clinical practice, it is designed for use by a trained clinician alongside a full assessment, and even then the guidance is to interpret the number rather than obey it. A "normal" result is not a clean bill of health and an abnormal one is not a diagnosis. If a result worries you, take it to a professional.

Biology, chemistry and laboratory results

Lab calculators — dilutions, molarity, cell counts, growth rates, protein conversions, gel recipes — depend on the assumptions of the protocol in front of you: the molar mass you are using, the purity of the reagent, the wavelength of your reader, whether a concentration is w/v or v/v. Each page states its own assumptions, and the units are printed next to every field so that a figure copied from a protocol goes in as printed.

These pages are built for bench work and teaching. They are not a validated quality system, and a result that will be reported as a regulated measurement should be produced by the method your laboratory validated, not by a public web page.

Construction, engineering and safety

Material, structural, electrical, plumbing and HVAC calculators give estimates from simplified models. Loads, tolerances, soil conditions and codes vary by jurisdiction, by product and by site. Anything that bears weight, conducts current, holds back water or resists fire needs a qualified professional and the manufacturer's own data.

If a number will be built into a structure, connected to mains power or used to size a safety system, a calculator on a website is a first estimate at best — never the final word.

Legal and regulatory results

Date arithmetic, deadline calculators, statutory-interest figures and similar tools reproduce general rules. A deadline that matters — a filing, an appeal, a notice period — depends on your jurisdiction, the court, the agreement and the way the rule is served on you. Confirm it with the court, the authority or a lawyer. Using this site does not create a professional relationship of any kind.

Conversions and units

Unit conversions are exact where the definition is exact and rounded where the definition is a convention: an inch is exactly 25.4 millimetres, a US gallon is exactly 3.785411784 litres, a calorie has more than one definition and a tonne can be metric or imperial. Pages that involve a conventional unit state which one they use. If a figure must be exact for trade, use the definition your jurisdiction requires.

What the results are not

  • They are not personalised: no calculator here knows your full circumstances.
  • They are not current in real time: a tax band or a rate changes, and a page is corrected when someone notices.
  • They are not a professional opinion, and reading one does not create a professional relationship.
  • They are not a guarantee: where a page is found to be wrong, it is fixed — but you should not rely on any figure for anything that cannot be undone.

How to check a result yourself

Every calculator page prints the formula it used and a worked example with real numbers, so the first check is available on the page. If the worked example and the result disagree, the page is wrong — tell us. Beyond that: compare against a second independent source, sanity-check the order of magnitude, and read the assumptions section before acting on a number that looks surprising.

Reporting a problem

A wrong result is a bug, not a limitation, and it is treated as one. Send the calculator name, the values you entered and the answer you expected through the contact form, and if you know where the correct answer comes from — a textbook, a standard, a statement — say so. Those reports are how this page's caveats get shorter over time.
